cities.d: also known as Ouaga (pronounced "wa-ga"), is the capital city. It has several museums, and a major annual film festival

x.around: Ougadougou is a very orderly and clean city, and the traffic is very civilized. The city has a grid-based street system. There are traffic lights everywhere and motorists actually obey them. The people here are proud of their country and create a good impression. ===By taxi=== Ouagadougou is serviced by two types of taxi: white and green. White taxis are rarer, more expensive, and exclusive.

hidden.d: Small garden with a statue depicting a woman handling a calabash to pour water. The 6-m (20-ft) high statue faces the railway station, welcoming travellers into Ouaga.

Urban park in Zone du Bois (also called 'La Foret') has many trails for walking and running. It also has a small zoo inside (CFA 100-200 for entrance) Bring binoculars to help you spot the crocodiles in the marsh near the bridge!…
Exhibits all the musical instruments of Burkina Faso.
Features enormous granite slabs that were designed by various sculptors. The exhibit displays works of art from five continents.
Museum complex devoted to the many local cultures, but most of the buildings are empty. It is on the east end of the city and is open seven days a week.

x.intro: Ouagadougou (pronounced: WA-ga-DOO-goo) is the capital of Burkina Faso and the nation's cultural and economic centre. Its name is informally shortened to Ouaga.

must.d: Built by the French in the 1930s, it is one of the largest in western Africa. The architecture is reminiscent of a European romanesque basilica, but intentionally evokes the impression of incompleteness due to its two steeples of…

n.es: Catedral de la Inmaculada Concepción de Uagadugú

x.safe: Loads of touts, purse snatchers and faux types at the Grand Marche. Don't go without local assistance.

cities.d: home to the famous Banfora Cascades
the nation's second largest city is a major center of culture and music

x.around: However, you are at a distinct disadvantage when it comes to negotiation if you are white, and if you can afford to get to Burkina Faso XOF500 is hardly bank breaking.

hidden.d: A fine example of Sahel-style mud architecture, the mosque was built by a local king to uphold his side of a bargain.

x.intro: With a population of more than half a million, Bobo-Dioulasso is the second largest city in Burkina Faso, and is a major center of culture and music. The city has many historic buildings reflecting its complex past.

cities.d: hosts a biennial festival of masks
hardly a pleasant town, Gaoua is near the Ruins of Loropéni, a UNESCO World Heritage site.

x.around: Taxis make a killing here compared to other parts of the country. From the gare to the center it costs 300 CFA. However if you are going further than the centreville (i.e. le desert or the campement allemand) it is 500 CFA.
x.intro: Gaoua is a market town in the Black Volta Region of Burkina Faso.

must.d: With imposing stone wall this ruined fortress is the best preserved of about ten in the area. Believed to be at least a thousand years old and is yet to be fully excavated. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2009.

cities.d: home of the Royal Palace of Issouka, an example of earthen architecture

x.intro: Koudougou is the second largest city in the Volta Delta of Burkina Faso.

cities.d: the entry point to Burkina from Mali

x.intro: Ouahigouya is a large town in North Burkina Faso, near the Mali border. It is the fourth largest city in Burkina, and as the final major city in Burkina on the route to Mali, there is a constant flow of tourists and commercial travelers.

cities.d: home of the Botanical Garden Bantia, and gateway to the national parks of the southeast

x.intro: Fada n'Gourma is a city in East Burkina Faso, capital of the Region Est and Province Gourma, as well as seat of the king of Gulmu (i.e. Gourma).

cities.d: town in the northern part of the country, and an important market for cattle, sheep, goats

x.intro: Djibo is in North Burkina Faso. Djibo is pretty dry and dusty, with a lake. The population is predominantly Peul and thus Fulfulde is predominantly spoken and élévage is important. This is the capital of the Soum province. There is a substantial Mossi population with some others sprinkled in (Koroumba, Bella).
x.safe: See the warning on the Burkina Faso article for information on the security situation.

other.d: a transborder park and UNESCO World Heritage Site shared with Niger and Benin

x.intro: W National Park is a trans-border park, with the most important areas in Southwestern Niger, around a meander in the River Niger shaped like the letter W.
x.safe: Caution recommended given rising destabilisation and unrest in eastern Burkina Faso since 2018. As of 2024, Niger is also unsafe due to civil unrest.
